assessment.rationale: Spans state that RFC 9110 (June 2022) defines safe and idempotent methods, and that idempotency allows automatic retry after failures. The table in span 130 lists safe methods (e.g., GET, HEAD) and confirms they are idempotent. This directly supports the claim.
assessment.synthesis_coverage: Covers definition of safe and idempotent methods in RFC 9110 as of June 2022
assessment.provenance_note: Source cites RFC 9110 section 9 as the origin of method classifications

excerpts.text:
RFC 9110 section 9 defines eight methods and classifies each as safe (read only in intent) and idempotent (repeating it has the same intended effect as sending it once):

| Method | Purpose | Safe | Idempotent |
RFC 9110 explains that idempotent requests "can be repeated automatically if a communication failure occurs", and that a proxy "MUST NOT automatically retry non-idempotent requests".
